theme: Architecture and structure defects in a multi-project .NET fleet-maintenance system, and their look-alikes

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Infrastructure.Telematics
entries.rationale: The Domain project references the telematics adapter project FleetOps.Infrastructure.Telematics. ADR 0002 states that `src/FleetOps.Domain/` must not reference `src/FleetOps.Infrastructure/` (and any FleetOps.Infrastructure.* adapter); the dependency points outward from the innermost layer. The architecture test checks the Domain assembly only against the assemblies that existed when it was written, so it still passes.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The code half of LAY-001: a Domain type imports the telematics adapter namespace, the line the ADR's Domain-must-not-reference-Infrastructure rule forbids.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A domain service takes the HTTP telematics client (ITelematicsClient from the infrastructure adapter) and calls the vendor API from inside the domain to read live odometer values, instead of receiving the reading from the Application layer.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A controller injects FleetOpsDbContext and queries the database directly, bypassing the Application layer. ADR 0004 states that code under `src/FleetOps.Api/Controllers/` must not reference `src/FleetOps.Infrastructure/`. (Program.cs, the composition root, may: see TRP-006.)

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Diagnostics
entries.rationale: FleetOps.ServiceDefaults is the shared host-defaults library every host references (stable: 2 dependents, 1 dependency). It references FleetOps.Diagnostics, which itself references five projects (Contracts, Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Infrastructure.Telematics) and is referenced by nothing else in production: instability 5/6 = 0.83 over production edges. A stable package depends on the most volatile one (Stable Dependencies Principle); any change anywhere ripples into the shared defaults.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Infrastructure.Scheduling
entries.rationale: Namespace-level cycle (a project-reference cycle cannot exist in a solution that builds: NuGet restore rejects it, NU1108). FleetOps.Infrastructure.Scheduling uses Email (ReminderDispatcher -> ReminderMailer) and FleetOps.Infrastructure.Email uses Scheduling (ReminderMailer -> QuietHours). The site is the back edge, Email's import of Scheduling.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Notifications
entries.rationale: An empty shell project: a csproj with no source file, listed in the solution and referenced by nothing. Structural noise left from a feature that was never written.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Infrastructure
entries.rationale: FleetOps.Infrastructure is the grab-bag of every integration: persistence, e-mail, documents, fuel cards, tyres, parts, geocoding, scheduling, auditing and reporting - more than 120 public types across more than 10 namespaces with unrelated responsibilities that change for unrelated reasons. A reviewer asks for one adapter project per integration.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A pass-through layer: every WorkOrderFacade method forwards its arguments unchanged to the mediator and returns the result. It adds a hop (controller -> IWorkOrderFacade -> WorkOrderFacade -> ISender -> handler) and an interface, and no behaviour.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Business rules in a controller action: the status-transition check, labour pricing with an overtime rate, the parts markup and the manager-approval limit are computed in WorkOrdersController.Approve instead of in the Domain (WorkOrder) or an Application handler; no other entry point (the Worker, a test) can apply them. (v1.1.0: relabelled from the metric business-logic-share, used in v1.0.0 because no finding concept existed, to the finding concept business-logic-in-controller; same site.)

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: FuelPriceCache is registered as a singleton (through a factory, which also hides the mismatch from the container's scope validation) and keeps the IFuelCardTransactionStore it receives in its constructor; the store is registered scoped and wraps the scoped DbContext. The singleton captures one scoped store and DbContext for the life of the process.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: GeocodingCache is a singleton that reads and writes a plain Dictionary from concurrent requests without a lock; concurrent writes can corrupt the dictionary.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: IFleetReporting declares 17 unrelated report operations (costs, downtime, fuel, tyres, inspections, exports); its only consumer uses two of them.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Inspections slice holds a field of the WorkOrders slice's concrete OpenWorkOrderHandler and calls it directly, coupling two vertical slices that ADR 0003 says communicate only through the mediator.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A query handler (IQueryHandler<GetWorkOrderQuery, ...>) records 'last viewed' on the work order and saves it: reading a work order writes persistent state.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A checkable rule (slices under Features/ do not reference each other's types) declared with `enforcement: prose`; no architecture test or analyzer checks it, and SLC-001 shows it already broken.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The ADR claims `enforcement: test` with an enforcement_link to tests/FleetOps.ArchitectureTests/ControllerRulesTests.cs, which does not exist: the rule is enforced by nothing, and LAY-003 breaks it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Contracts
entries.rationale: FleetOps.Contracts is depended on by most projects and depends on nothing (instability 0). Being widely depended on is what a stable contracts package is for.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Contracts
entries.rationale: Concrete and stable (A=0, I=0) by design: wire DTO records cannot be abstract and change rarely, so the 'zone of pain' reading does not apply to a contracts package.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Application.Tests
entries.rationale: A test project referencing Infrastructure (to run handlers against the real repositories on in-memory SQLite). Test projects are not layers; nothing ships them.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.ArchitectureTests
entries.rationale: The architecture test project references every production project with code - it must load them to check them.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Infrastructure
entries.rationale: Infrastructure -> Domain is the allowed direction: infrastructure implements the domain's ports.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Program.cs is the composition root: it references every layer to wire dependency injection.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Api
entries.rationale: The API host project references Application, Infrastructure, Contracts and ServiceDefaults to compose them; a host is the outermost ring.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Dependency inversion: IVehicleRepository is declared in the Domain and implemented here. The domain owns the abstraction; nothing in the Domain references this class.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.Worker
entries.rationale: A thin but purposeful host: Program.cs plus one BackgroundService that sends the due-maintenance query on a schedule. Small because the work lives in Application.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A singleton that takes IServiceScopeFactory and creates a scope per run to resolve scoped services: the correct pattern, nothing is captured.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A singleton holding a TRANSIENT IReminderWindowCalculator that is stateless and not disposable. Keeping one instance of a stateless object is harmless (the container's own scope validation only rejects scoped services in singletons). Contested - see benchmark/README.md.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A singleton cache over ConcurrentDictionary: thread-safe by construction.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A singleton whose mutable list is read and replaced only inside lock blocks.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A composite of three small role interfaces (vehicles, work orders, inspections); it declares no member itself and consumers depend on the narrow roles. 18 inherited members are not a fat interface.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A slice handler holding fields of Domain types (IVehicleRepository, MaintenanceDueEvaluator): types outside every slice, not another slice's.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A query handler that populates an in-process memory cache, logs and increments a metric: none of it is persistent or observable domain state.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A decorator that looks like forwarding but adds behaviour: retries with back-off on transient HTTP failures.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A process decision (`enforcement: not-applicable`): there is nothing in code to enforce.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `enforcement: test` with a link to tests/FleetOps.ArchitectureTests/ContractsTests.cs, which exists and checks the rule completely (Contracts references no other FleetOps assembly).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The project-reference graph is acyclic. Api -> Application -> Domain and Api -> Infrastructure -> Domain form a diamond, not a cycle. (The one real cycle is between two namespaces, CYC-001.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FleetOps.ServiceDefaults
entries.rationale: A thin but purposeful library: the host defaults every FleetOps host shares (clock, JSON logging, health checks), the conventional ServiceDefaults shape. Folding it into a host would duplicate it in the other; its size is not a structural defect. (Its dependency on Diagnostics is SDP-001, a different concept.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: CA2007 (ConfigureAwait) is switched off at the repository root with its reason on the line above: tests must not call ConfigureAwait(false) (xUnit1030), and src/.editorconfig switches it back on as a warning for all production code. A scoped, documented suppression.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: One bounded context (fleet maintenance). Layers and projects of one context are not contexts, so no type crosses a context boundary.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: The system publishes no events: the Contracts records are request/response DTOs and summaries (VehicleSummary, MaintenanceDue, ...), not messages announcing something that happened.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Coupling posture: no project cycle, one stable library depending on a volatile one (SDP-001) and one outward layer reference (LAY-001) among ten production projects; a moderate deduction.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: src/ + tests/, one solution, ten production projects that build, but one empty shell project (SHL-001).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One oversized project (GOD-001) among ten production projects; the rest are small.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Controllers reach handlers through a pass-through facade plus the mediator (IND-001); otherwise direct. Wide band: indirection metrics vary.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: A recognisable clean/layered architecture with vertical slices and CQRS in the Application layer; heavier than a system this size needs, but consistent.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: By design the glue dominates: the Infrastructure god module is the largest project and pricing/approval rules sit in a controller; Domain + Application are well under half of production lines.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: src/ and tests/ separation, every project under the FleetOps root namespace.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Model-judged. Handlers follow one Mediator shape, but controllers mix three conventions (mediator, facade, DbContext). Wide band for judge variance.
